- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish bias.  
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1-2 days); apply a 1-2 day lag correction to dampen immediate post-spike forecasts.  
- In 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates mean-reversion trends; add a small upward bias (e.g., +0.5–1.5%) if recent 7-day average is below 30-day average.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in adjusting; apply a 3–5 day “sentiment catch-up” adjustment to forecast.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, avoid extreme outliers (e.g., >10% deviation from recent 14-day moving average); cap or smooth extreme highs/lows.
